authority-scope.name: authority-coverage
authority-scope.claim: The change to {surface} satisfies every governing authority requirement bearing on {category} for {obligation_id}
authority-scope.counterexample: The change to {surface} violates or omits a governing authority requirement bearing on {category} for {obligation_id}

behavioral-correctness.name: behavioral-equivalence
behavioral-correctness.claim: The change to {surface} produces the intended behavior for {category} on all inputs reachable through {obligation_id}
behavioral-correctness.counterexample: There exists a reachable input for which the change to {surface} produces wrong behavior for {category} on {obligation_id}

test-adequacy.name: test-adequacy
test-adequacy.claim: Tests covering {surface} would fail if the changed behavior for {category} regressed on {obligation_id}
test-adequacy.counterexample: A regression in the changed behavior for {category} on {surface} would pass the current tests for {obligation_id}

security-privacy.name: security-boundary
security-privacy.claim: The change to {surface} introduces no new security or privacy exposure for {category} on {obligation_id}
security-privacy.counterexample: The change to {surface} creates a security or privacy exposure for {category} on {obligation_id}

reliability-concurrency.name: failure-interleaving
reliability-concurrency.claim: The change to {surface} preserves reliability and concurrency invariants for {category} under failure and interleaving on {obligation_id}
reliability-concurrency.counterexample: Some failure or interleaving breaks the change to {surface} for {category} on {obligation_id}

compatibility-migration.name: compatibility-preservation
compatibility-migration.claim: The change to {surface} preserves compatibility and migration safety for {category} on {obligation_id}
compatibility-migration.counterexample: The change to {surface} breaks a consumer or migration path for {category} on {obligation_id}

performance-resources.name: resource-bound
performance-resources.claim: The change to {surface} keeps resource use within existing bounds for {category} on {obligation_id}
performance-resources.counterexample: The change to {surface} exceeds existing resource bounds for {category} on {obligation_id}

operability-configuration.name: operability-surface
operability-configuration.claim: The change to {surface} keeps the system operable and correctly configured for {category} on {obligation_id}
operability-configuration.counterexample: The change to {surface} degrades operability or misconfigures {category} on {obligation_id}

documentation-contract.name: documentation-fidelity
documentation-contract.claim: Documentation and declared contracts remain accurate for {surface} under {category} on {obligation_id}
documentation-contract.counterexample: Documentation or a declared contract is now inaccurate for {surface} under {category} on {obligation_id}

source-custody.name: custody-integrity
source-custody.claim: The change to {surface} edits only sources it owns and preserves canonical custody for {category} on {obligation_id}
source-custody.counterexample: The change to {surface} edits a downstream or foreign-custody source for {category} on {obligation_id}

high_risk_extra_families.name: adversarial-witness
high_risk_extra_families.claim: No honestly-produced artifact can make {surface} appear to satisfy {category} while it does not for {obligation_id}
high_risk_extra_families.counterexample: An honestly-produced artifact could make {surface} appear to satisfy {category} while it does not for {obligation_id}

high_risk_extra_families.name: rollback-containment
high_risk_extra_families.claim: If the change to {surface} is wrong for {category}, the failure is contained and reversible on {obligation_id}
high_risk_extra_families.counterexample: A wrong change to {surface} for {category} is not contained or not reversible on {obligation_id}
